'''Lenore Alice Epstein Bixby''' (August 12, 1914 – April 5, 1994)<ref name="ssdi">''Social Security Death Index, 1935-2014''. [[Social Security Administration]].</ref> was an American statistician who worked with the [[Social Security Administration]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences]].{{r|buff|wapo}}

==Education==
She was born in [[Buffalo, New York]],{{r|buff}} and some of her earlier publications are listed under that name.{{r|epubs}} As a student of the class of 1935 at [[Wellesley College]], she became chairman of the school's branch of the [[League of Women Voters]], and graduated [[Phi Beta Kappa]] with honors as a Senior Durant Scholar.{{r|legenda}}
She did graduate study in [[economics]] and [[statistics]] at [[Columbia University]], earning a master's degree there in 1937.{{r|wapo}}

==Career==
After completing her studies, she came to work for the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] and then, after [[World War II]], as an operations officer for the [[Marshall Plan]]. This work took her away from Washington to [[Paris]].
She joined the Social Security Administration in 1954,{{r|wapo}}
and worked there as deputy assistant commissioner of the Office of Research and Statistics and later as director of the Division of Retirement and Survivors' Studies.{{r|buff|wapo}}
While there, she married F. Lovell Bixby, a prominent [[penologist]], who died in 1975.{{r|buff|wapo|bixob}}

She retired from the administration in 1977,{{r|wapo}} but continued to work as a statistician for the National Academy of Sciences, in their Committee on National Statistics.{{r|buff|wapo}}

==Awards and honors==
In 1969, she was honored by the [[American Statistical Association]], who elected her as one of their [[fellow]]s.{{r|fasa|wapo}} She was also a fellow of the Gerontological Society.{{r|wapo}} She was a founding member of the National Academy of Social Insurance.{{r|nasi}}
